rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same Schedule SE line 13 (Step 2 copies it); sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. Both use this person's own Schedule SE line 13 (Pub. 560 p. 39, Step 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C and otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c (i1040sse p. 2, line 4c; 'If less than $400 ... you don't owe self-employment tax'), which gives zero for the same person. Church employee income, optional methods, statutory employees and notaries are refused on both sides (person.se_screen, sc.statutory). Both then take one-half of the self-employment tax (Pub. 560 chapter 5, Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed, step 2).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal representation; project retained. The instruction says that if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20 the excess cannot be claimed on the return and the employer should adjust it, otherwise Form 843 (i1040gi p. 117). The project refuses the return on that condition and on railroad (RRTA) compensation through the line's `refuses` entries; the second transcription returns a zero credit. The project's reading is the spec's refusal policy (spec 2.2, 2.5); within the non-refused scope the credit agrees (eligible: more than one employer and wages over the base; excess over the limit). Stage 13 re-run: the credit is figured separately for each spouse from that spouse's Forms W-2 (i1040gi p. 117), as both transcriptions do.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). Box 1 is the same on both sides. Line 1e goes to the only person whose Forms W-2 show box 10, or to the taxpayer when nobody's do, on both sides; when both spouses' do, the second now gives it to neither (and refuses, its h_dc_1e_split), where the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6): shown in the taxpayer's line 4 and refused when a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate). The self-employment part is the same on returns the tool completes: the second subtracts the Schedule SE deduction without a Schedule C guard (zero below the $400 floor, so the Schedule C result is used, as the project does when no Schedule SE is filed) and leaves out statutory employee income, which is refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory). i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Box 1 and the self-employment part are the same on both sides: the self-employment part differs only as person.eic_se does (the project's zero for a person with no Schedule C against the second's $400 floor, and the second's exclusion of statutory employee income, which is refused by sc.statutory), and both use Schedule C profit or loss when no Schedule SE is filed (p503 p. 11, Self-employment earnings, "Include your self-employment earnings in earned income, even if they are less than $400 and you didn't file Schedule SE"). Line 1e goes to the only person on a return that is not joint and to the one spouse whose Forms W-2 show box 10 on both sides. The sides differ only when both spouses' Forms W-2 show box 10: the second counts line 1e in both spouses' earned income, so it counts it twice; the project follows the binding reading amb.2025.dc_line1e_attribution (owner decision 6), refusing when line 1e is above zero and a credit remains (f2441.attrib_gate) and otherwise showing it in the taxpayer's line 4, where it cannot change the credit. i2441 p. 4, Lines 4 and 5, "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately".

Both are W-2 box 1 plus the self-employment part, without line 1e (i2441 p. 5, Line 18, "for purposes of lines 18 and 19, earned income doesn't include any dependent care benefits shown on line 12"). The self-employment part differs only as on person.dc_earned: the second has no Schedule C guard and leaves out statutory employee income, refused by sc.statutory; below the $400 floor its Schedule SE deduction is zero, which gives the Schedule C result, as the project uses when no Schedule SE is filed.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 93, Line 11: "If you were an eligible educator in 2025, you can deduct on line 11 up to $300 of qualified expenses you paid in 2025." Both lines give the smaller of the expenses and $300 for an eligible educator and zero otherwise; they differ only in which of the two dispositive questions is asked first. The project asks person.eligible_educator only when person.educator_expenses is more than zero, so the candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f2441.2.deepseek) are interview records with zero expenses and no eligibility answer, where the candidate needs eligibility the text does not need but also permits asking; the project-unknown records are partial records withholding the expenses with eligibility false (partial classm.f8889.2.deepseek, classm.asset.1, classm.carloan.1 -educator_expenses), where the candidate's zero is right and the project asks expenses first. No value differs on any record where both are supplied. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,363 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 1249 candidate-unknown, 35 project-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi EIC Worksheet B, Part 1 and Part 2 (Schedule SE line 3 less line 13 if you file Schedule SE, otherwise Schedule C line 31), with i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The candidate uses line 3 less line 13 when line 4a is $400 or more, else the Schedule C total; the project uses the same choice keyed on line 6 more than zero. Same value wherever both evaluate. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Otherwise the same Schedule SE computation; church employee income, the optional methods and statutory employee income are refused (person.se_screen, sc.statutory), so the second's sums over all of the person's Schedules C (it no longer excludes statutory employee income) select the same entries as the project's. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides. EIC Worksheet B Part 1 for a person filing Schedule SE and Part 2 otherwise on both sides (i1040gi p. 47).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2: "Divide the refigured contribution limit from Step 1 equally between you and your spouse, unless you both agree on a different allocation (such as allocating nothing to one spouse)." i8889 p. 7, Step 3: "Subtract the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1." Unknown kind: The candidate sums f8889.share, the published field that carries the f8889.allocation_bad refusal; that gate reads household.hsa_share_sum, which sums person.hsa_share, so the candidate's line depends on itself ("cycle at person[spouse].hsa_share", "cycle at household.hsa_share_sum"; classm.f8889.1, classm.f8889.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.2) whenever the gate evaluates its agreed-allocation test. The published interface listed f8889.share_raw and f8889.share by id, form and type only, with no label or dependency, so the candidate could not tell the pre-check share from the checked one; the source reading (each spouse's part under Steps 2 and 3) is the one the project encodes with share_raw. Value kind: representation; the differences are non-split forms (classm.asset.1 $356.25 against $0.00, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8880.4, classm.f8959.2, classm.ltc.1, classm.sc.1), and person.hsa_step1 and person.hsa_share feed only household.hsa_step1_sum and household.hsa_share_sum, which are read only in the third disjunct of f8889.allocation_bad (agreed allocation with different Step 1 limits or more than Step 1 allocated). That gate is reached only through f8889.share on a form with f8889.split true; if only one spouse's form is split, household.hsa_split_count is 1 and the gate is already true; if both are split, the project's split filter keeps both forms and the unfiltered sum is the same (one form per person, more than one refused by person.hsa_repeated). So the filtered and unfiltered sums cannot give a different printed amount. Refusal kind: representation; the candidate surfaces f8889.allocation_bad one level up on returns the project refuses at f8889.share and line 6 anyway (gen#84: household.hsa_split_count 1; stage13.refuse.hsa_family_one_spouse, stage13.refuse.hsa_mixed_methods). kinds_by_return places 2 candidate refusals on returns the full interview completes (not among the recorded witnesses); they follow from the same field choice, the candidate reaching f8889.allocation_bad through f8889.share on a form the project never reads it for, and are covered by the interface-gap ruling. A distribution is refused on both sides (f8606.dist; the second's person.ira_dist_gate).

The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc) and asks person.plan only then: i1040gi p. 93, Line 16, "If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Where the second caps each contribution at its limit (the SEP at Step 21; SIMPLE employer contributions at the matching or 2% maximum, salary reductions at $16,500 and catch-up at its limit and compensation), the project enters the contributions and refuses any amount above the limits (person.sep_excess, person.simple_excess, and the plan screen's 'contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount'), so the caps never bind on a return the project admits; the second's compensation, profit times 92.35% without the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, is never below the project's, so it admits no less. The project also enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.has_sc), and asks person.plan only then; a person without a Schedule C is not self-employed in scope (partnership and farm income refused by scope.schedule1), and 'If you were self-employed or a partner, you may be able to take this deduction' (i1040gi p. 93). Evaluated stage14.simple.match_age50 ($19,662.30) and stage14.simple.nonelective_60 ($22,858.20): the second's formula gives the same amounts.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained (as the prior ruling). W-2 box 12 deferrals and voluntary contributions are the same on both sides. For the person's own SIMPLE salary reductions the project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C (person.plan is asked only then) and counts the whole deferral, catch-up included, refusing amounts above the limits (person.simple_excess); the second now caps the deferral at $16,500 (ret.simple_limit) because it refuses catch-up contributions rather than figuring them. A catch-up contribution is an elective deferral: f8880 p. 2, Line 2, "Elective deferrals ... to a 401(k), 403(b), governmental 457(b), SEP, SIMPLE, or the federal TSP".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.

The project enters zero for a person with no Schedule C; the second applies the $400 floor of Schedule SE line 4c, which gives zero for the same person. Railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation on line 8a is refused for a person with a Schedule C (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 and 7 on both sides.

Church employee income, optional methods, statutory employees and notaries are refused on both sides (person.se_screen, sc.statutory). Otherwise both are one-half of line 12 (Schedule SE (2025), line 13).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same line; sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.json): 3,234 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 173 candidate-refuses, 1239 candidate-unknown, 1 project-refuses.
